text: Hey class, I'm Beeswax, your unbeelievably charming and handsome bee assistant.
Bees are super important for our planet, and six things around you matter a lot to bees.
Walk up to one and take a look, and if you have a question, just say "Hey Beeswax" and I'll bee right there.
Ooh, you found a bee fact. Would you like to hear it?
I'll take that as a yes.
Don't worry, I'll bee right here if you need anything.

label: native_flower
text: You found a sunflower, and did you know it first grew wild in North America?

label: native_flower
text: Some scientists think one in three bites you eat is thanks to pollinators like me, which is pretty sweet.

label: native_flower
text: Your next adventure is the sunflower, so go find it.

label: honey_jar
text: That's honeycomb, and here's a sweet one: a pound of honey can take up to two million flower visits.

label: honey_jar
text: Just don't leave store honey out for bees, it can carry a bee germ called foulbrood, but it's fine on toast.

label: honey_jar
text: Now head to your next adventure, one big step to your left.

label: bug_spray
text: Hmm, that's bug spray, and when it gets on flowers, bees carry it home to the babies.

label: bug_spray
text: One study found US farmland got about forty-eight times more toxic for insects to eat in twenty-two years.

label: bug_spray
text: Your next adventure is one more step to your left, so brace yourself.

label: bee_hotel
text: Oh, you found a bee hotel, a safe little home for wild bees like mason bees.

label: bee_hotel
text: Nearly one in four kinds of wild bees scientists checked is in danger, and bee hotels help them hang on.

label: bee_hotel
text: Let's get away from that can, your next adventure is one step to your left.

label: pebble_dish
text: That's a bee water dish, and since bees can't swim, the pebbles are their little landing pads.

label: pebble_dish
text: On a hot day, bees haul home about eighty percent of their weight in water to cool the hive.

label: pebble_dish
text: Thirsty? Your next adventure is one step to your left.

label: beehive
text: That's a beehive, and last year beekeepers in the US lost about four in ten of their hives.

label: beehive
text: The year before it was more than half, the worst on record, and tiny mites spreading viruses are a big reason.

label: beehive
text: Last adventure, one step to your left, and it's the big one.
You found them all, and you've earned your Bee Scout badge!
Now you know that flowers feed us, honey takes millions of flower visits, and bug spray hurts bees.
So give bees a home and a drink, help save the hives, and thanks for the bee-autiful work, scout.
A little to your left.
A little to your right.
Come a little closer, bees are small and so are my eyes.
Lift your chin a little so I can see it.
Hmm, where'd you go? I'm a bee, not a bloodhound, so find the next picture for me.
Ask your teacher for another assignment.
